title: Annotatio IV §.XXIII: Wren’s Jude 19 elenchus — psychikoi without spirit; they ban spiritual presence, chase only psychic ratio
pass_a_gloss: And this now is that fight which they shout — from whose dream-fiction they truly thrust themselves into that Elenchus of the Apostle (now pertaining to no one ever more than to themselves): ‘these are they who separate themselves, psychikoi, not having the spirit,’ Jude v. 19. For when they themselves execrate every Spiritual presence of the Lord’s body, and miserably immersed in matter alone taste nothing beyond sense, and chase no ratio in the sacrament except the natural and psychic one, they strongly show themselves already as those who separate — whether that be interpreted of Things (for they order the better ratio of the Sacrament, which is Spiritual and truly Divine, to be wholly banished) or of Persons (and then they either exclude themselves — and so the Latin Vulgar and ours render it — plainly after the manner of the Gentiles, believing no more than they can attain from natural light, or rather twilight; or at least they hope they can drive Us from Divine Participation).
pass_b_english: Wren turns their dream-fight into Jude 19’s elenchus: they are the separators — psychikoi without the spirit — now more than anyone.

Immersed in matter alone, they execrate every spiritual presence of the Lord’s body, chase only a natural/psychic sacrament-ratio, and either banish the spiritual-divine ratio of the sacrament or exclude themselves (and hope to drive us) from divine participation — Gentile-style, believing only natural twilight.
source_text: Atque hæc jam illa pugna est, quam clamitant, è cujus sibi per somnium fictione, verè sese protrudunt in Elenchum illum Apostoli (ad neminem unquam magis, quam ad ipsos nunc pertinentem,) etoi eisin hoi apodiorizontes, psychikoi, pneuma mē echontes, Judæ vers. 19. Spiritualem enim omnem corporis Dominici præsentiam cùm ipsi execrentur, & materiæ soli miserè immersi, ultra sensum nihil sapiant, nullamque nisi naturalem, atque psychikēn rationem in sacramento sectentur, fortiter sese jam apodiorizontas præstant, sive illud de Rebus interpretandum sit, Potiorem enim Sacramenti rationem, & quæ Spiritualis veréque Divina est, prorsus exulare jubent; sive de Personis, & tum vel semetipsos excludunt (& à Latino quidem Vulgari, Nostrisque sic redditur:) Ethnicorum planè more, non plùs credentes, quàm ex naturali lumine, seu potiùs crepusculo, assequi possunt; vel saltem, posse se Nos exterminare à Participio Divino sperant.
